title: Throughput & Latency Scaling Playbook — Brainstorm
content:
Meeting: Ad-hoc architecture brainstorm to synthesize RFC proposals into an operational playbook for throughput/latency scaling
Date: 2024-02-12 (notes updated 2024-02-20)
Attendees: Priya Nair (chair), Liam O'Connor, Jasmin Park, Marco Silva, Elena Ivanova, Samir Patel
Purpose: Decide a pragmatic, testable playbook for how the serving runtime reacts to changing load and tail-latency incidents. Bring together recent RFC fragments (dynamic batching knobs, autoscaler sizing, cold-start mitigations, fallback routing) and record decisions and next steps for an RFC that can be published.

TL;DR decisions (high level)
- Adopt a two-tier autoscaling policy: "stable" (predictive, slower scale up/down) + "burst" (fast scale-up with short TTL) to handle sudden spikes while limiting churn.
- Make batching window adaptive by per-tenant sequence-length histogram and per-slot vacancy; default target latency SLA is 150ms p50 for small-req workflows and 300ms p95 across mixed workloads.
- Implement a cold-start warmers subsystem for private/de-dicated deployments (warmers + KV prefetch) and a conservative fallback to smaller model-variants for hosted tier during hard cold-starts.
- Introduce a lightweight routing policy for cost-tiered fallbacks that prefers cheaper quantized variants on background/batch workloads but keeps full-precision variants for interactive SLOs.

Context & motivation
- Multiple postmortems and monitoring spikes show recurring tail-latency events when sudden load changes coincide with cold pods and fragmented KV cache hit rates. Current autoscaler reacts too slowly in some cases and causes head-of-line amplification in batching windows.
- Teams have partially-complete RFCs: adaptive batching strategy (Jasmin), two-stage autoscaler (Liam), warmers & kv-prefetch (Marco), quantized fallback routing (Elena). This meeting stitches them into operational steps.

Detailed discussion notes
1) Autoscaling (Liam + Priya)
   - Two-tier approach: predictive stable pool sized by rolling 24h quantiles for each tenancy class + burst pool that can accept requests for a short TTL (configurable, default 90s).
   - Burst pool should use pre-warmed instances if available. If not, requests are allowed to queue behind the existing serving slots but subject to request-queue length limits to avoid unbounded head-of-line blocking.
   - Metrics to monitor: scale-up latency, scale-down aggression, and request drop rate. Add health check for model load completion (not just container readiness).

2) Adaptive batching (Jasmin)
   - Make per-slot batching window a function of three signals: observed seq-length distribution, target latency budget for that model/route, and current concurrency per-slot.
   - Heuristic: if p50 seq < 64 and target p50 latency < 200ms -> small-window (4-8ms). Otherwise increase window up to 40ms for throughput.
   - Need an initial rollout experiment: A/B route where 10% of production traffic uses adaptive window with conservative knobs. Track token cost/unit, tail latency, and throughput.

3) Cold-start & warmers (Marco)
   - Warmers approach: maintain a warm pool for hot models (user-configurable TTL). Warmers should populate KV cache for expected prefixes (startup prompts, common system tokens).
   - For private deployments we can offer scheduled warm periods tied to customer traffic patterns. For hosted tier, run a cheap sampler to keep a small fraction of pods warm during predicted peaks.
   - Action: prototype an on-demand KV-prefetch API and an internal warmers controller that triggers after scale actions.

4) Model-variant fallback & routing (Elena)
   - Define semantics for fallback: trivial fallback chain is {full-fp -> quantized-4bit -> smaller-arch}. Routing decision uses SLO, cost budget, and tenant policy.
   - Must preserve determinism for critical business workflows (customer can pin no-fallback). Default should be safe: try quantized variant with quality monitor and auto-rollback on regression.
   - Add observable: per-request variant-used metadata in traces for downstream eval.

5) Safety & QoS considerations (Samir)
   - Rate-limit combined with budget tokens per-tenant. Define hard and soft thresholds; soft threshold triggers best-effort fallbacks, hard threshold returns 429 or prioritizes higher-tier customers.
   - Graceful error semantics: when variant fallback fails quality checks, perform automatic rollback and route to a lower-latency region if available.

Experiments & acceptance criteria
- Experiment A (adaptive batching): 2-week A/B test on mixed-chat route. Acceptance: p95 latency does not regress >10% while token-throughput improves >8% and cost/token decreases by >=3% for the test group.
- Experiment B (two-tier autoscaler): synthetic spike tests + shadowing on production traffic for 48h. Acceptance: median scale-up time for burst pool < 30s and request-drop rate < 0.1% under spike profile.
- Experiment C (warmers): simulate cold-start profile for top-10 models; acceptance: cold-start tail (p99) latency improvement >= 2x for warmed pods vs baseline.
- Experiment D (fallback routing): run controlled canary that shifts 5% of traffic to quantized variant. Success if quality regression (measured via eval prompts) < 1% and downstream error rate unaffected.

Open questions / risks
- KV cache consistency across slot migration: if sessions move between pods, we need a clear contract on whether we rebuild the cache or fetch from shared hotstore. Tradeoff: rebuild latency vs cross-node transfer cost.
- Billing and telemetry: tagging fallback variant use has cost implications and must be surfaced on invoices — need finance input (create INF-4305).
- Cross-region fallback complexity: latency of fallback to another region may negate benefits. Need region-aware policies.
- Quantization regressions: require pre-defined eval suites per model; who owns the suites? Research/Applied ML needs a central registry.

Action items (owner, ticket / ETA)
- Priya: Draft RFC combining these decisions into a playbook doc + rollout plan (INF-4316) — ETA 2024-02-23.
- Jasmin: Implement adaptive-batching prototype and set up A/B test harness (GH: runtime#814) — ETA 2024-03-08.
- Liam: Autoscaler bump & burst pool controller prototype (JIRA INF-4322) — ETA 2024-03-01.
- Marco: Warmers prototype + KV-prefetch API spec (JIRA INF-4331) — ETA 2024-03-10.
- Elena: Define variant fallback policy schema and telemetry fields (INF-4340) — ETA 2024-02-28.
- Samir: Draft QoS token model and billing impact note (work with finance) (INF-4305) — ETA 2024-03-05.

Notes to reviewers (informal)
- This doc is intentionally a synthesis — not all concrete knobs are finalized. The goal is to get alignment on the playbook and run narrow experiments. Expect further follow-ups where we pin exact latency windows and numeric thresholds.
- If you have existing benchmarks or customer cases that contradict the acceptance criteria above, drop links in the Confluence page before the RFC deadline.

Next meeting
- 2024-02-26 10:00am PT (sync to review RFC draft and experiment instrumentation checklist).

Raw snippets / ideas captured in jam session
- "burst TTL should be configurable per infra pool, default 90s, but allow 300s for long-running batch windows"
- "consider slot affinity hints to reduce kv-cache thrash when migrating sessions"
- "we could expose an operator-mode: pre-warm for scheduled events (customer-led) vs autonomous warmers"
- "instrumentation: variant_used tag should be searchable in logs and trace sampling prioritized for fallback incidents"

References (quick)
- Adaptive batching RFC (draft): GH issue runtime#789
- Autoscaler two-stage notes: slack thread /infra-runtime Feb 7
- Cold-start postmortem: INF-postmortem-2024-01-coldstart (Confluence)

End of notes.
